div.head: Quadr Ded 13
div.ab: Feliciora fuisse tempora nec tantis egena plusculis pernitiosa curiositate, circumferunt, tanquam tempus — quod est distensio quedam anni, que per attencionem presentium, per memoriam preteritorum, per expectacionem futurorum distinguitur — puram benefaciendi uoluntatem inpediat, et non magis prauis moribus inputandum quicquid a Deo per inobedientiam et dissimilitudinem preuaricationis alienat suggestione, delectatione, consensu, sine octo principalibus uitiis, quæ sunt gastrimargia (id est uentris ingluuies), fornicatio, tristicia, uana gloria, inuidia, ira, superbia (principium iræ Dei), malorum radix et antiqua nostri generis inimica, quæ cum numquam appetat quod conuenit, numquam uidet quod expedit.

div.ab: They put it about that times were happier and not in need of so many extras through pernicious curiosity, as though time — which is a certain extension of the year [?] (perhaps for animi, of the mind), which is distinguished by attention to present things, by memory of past things, by expectation of future things — should hinder the pure will to do good, and as though whatever estranges a man from God through disobedience and the unlikeness of transgression, by suggestion, delight, consent, were not rather to be imputed to depraved morals, or [?] to the eight principal vices, which are gastrimargia (that is, gluttony of the belly), fornication, sadness, vainglory, envy, anger, pride (the beginning of God's wrath), the root of evils and the ancient enemy of our race, which, since it never desires what is fitting, never sees what is expedient.
